# Finding the Antiderivative of $-x^5\sin(3x)$

## Method: Integration by Parts (Tabular Method)

I first compute $\int x^5\sin(3x)\,dx$ using the tabular method, then negate the result.

**Differentiation column** (powers of $x^5$):

| Sign | Derivative | Integral of $\sin(3x)$ |
|------|-----------|----------------------|
| + | $x^5$ | $-\dfrac{\cos(3x)}{3}$ |
| − | $5x^4$ | $-\dfrac{\sin(3x)}{9}$ |
| + | $20x^3$ | $\dfrac{\cos(3x)}{27}$ |
| − | $60x^2$ | $\dfrac{\sin(3x)}{81}$ |
| + | $120x$ | $-\dfrac{\cos(3x)}{243}$ |
| − | $120$ | $-\dfrac{\sin(3x)}{729}$ |

## Multiplying diagonals:

$$\int x^5\sin(3x)\,dx = -\frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3} + \frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9} + \frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27} - \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27} - \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81} + \frac{40\sin(3x)}{243}$$

## Negating for our integral:

$$\int -x^5\sin(3x)\,dx = \frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3} - \frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9} - \frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27} + \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27} + \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81} - \frac{40\sin(3x)}{243} + C$$

## Verification:

Differentiating term by term, all intermediate terms cancel, leaving exactly $-x^5\sin(3x)$ ✓
